lines.japanese: 「お前マジかよ春希！」
lines.english: “Are you serious, Haruki?!”

lines.japanese:
「あの小木曽雪菜がお前らのバンドに入ったって！？」

「一体なにがどうなってんだよ？　てかどうやって口説いた？」

「それ以前にお前、いつ小木曽さんと話ができるような関係になったんだよ！」

「俺……お前を尊敬するわ。その、チャンスを絶対に逃さない根回しの才能に」

「……みんな、頼むから俺に昼飯を食わせてくれ」

　昼休みの３年Ｅ組の教室に、周囲の喧騒をものともしないほどに大きく、それこそ耳をつんざくような怒号が鳴り響いていた。
lines.english:
“Setsuna Ogiso joined your band?!”

“What the hell happened? More importantly, how did you talk her into it?”

“No, before that—when did you even get on speaking terms with Ogiso?”

“I respect you, man. That talent for working every angle and never letting an opportunity slip by.”

“Please. All of you. Just let me eat my lunch.”

In Class 3-E at lunchtime, the shouting did not so much mingle with the surrounding din as overpower it—and threatened to split every eardrum in the room.

lines.japanese:
「いや、でもマジで驚天動地だろそれ」

「お前、小木曽だぞ？　三年連続ミス峰城大付だぞ？」

「いや、まだ三年目の投票終わってないから」

「マジでどうやって騙くらかしたんだよ……」

「だからそれは……じゃなくて騙してない。どさくさに紛れて人を貶めるな」

　この、言葉に詰まりながらも説教を忘れない、周囲の男子生徒たちにいつも鬱陶親しまれている少年の名前は北原春希という。

　なお、この『鬱陶親しまれる』というのは、とある親友が彼を評しての造語だが、春希にとってみればその内容よりも日本語の間違いが我慢ならなかった。
lines.english:
“No, seriously, that’s earth-shattering.”

“This is Ogiso we’re talking about. Miss Houjou High three years running!”

“This year’s voting isn’t over yet.”

“Seriously, how did you con her…?”

“I keep telling you, I—no. I did not con her. Don’t take advantage of the confusion to slander me.”

This boy, stuck for words yet constitutionally incapable of letting bad behavior pass without a lecture, was Haruki Kitahara, the perennial object of his male classmates’ “annoyection.”

The coinage belonged to a certain best friend who had invented it to describe him.

Haruki found the assault on the language harder to forgive than the sentiment behind it.

lines.japanese:
「なんか駄目元で軽～く頼んでみたら軽～く引き受けてくれたぞ？　みんな最初から諦めてただけじゃないのか？」

「ないない、絶対ない」

「お前、今まであのコに告って撃沈した英霊の数を知ってるか？」

「いや、知らないけど」

「ああ、俺も知らない」

「なんだよそれ」

「確かに死者の数は多すぎて誰も知らないけどさ。でも生還した英雄の数なら誰でも知ってるぞ。ゼロだ」

「だからお前らそれプロポーズ（申し出）の内容が全然違うだろ……」

　それはともかく、今、彼らの話題を独占している“あの小木曽雪菜”は、名を……当然ながら小木曽雪菜という。
lines.english:
“I asked her casually, expecting nothing, and she said yes like it was nothing. Maybe everyone else just gave up without trying.”

“No way. Absolutely no way.”

“Do you even know how many valiant souls have confessed to her and fallen in battle?”

“No. Why would I?”

“Neither do I.”

“Then what was the point of asking?”

“There are too many dead for anyone to count. But everyone knows how many heroes came home alive. Zero.”

“It wasn’t that kind of proposal, you idiots…”

Setting all that aside, the “Setsuna Ogiso” presently monopolizing their conversation was named—unsurprisingly—Setsuna Ogiso.

lines.japanese:
“とある事情”で、春希が三年生になって初めて言葉を交わし、そしてもしかしたらそれ以上に関わることになるかもしれない相手……

　ぶっちゃけ、春希の所属する軽音楽同好会の新メンバー。

　一月後に控えた学園祭用の即席バンドの、さらに即席ボーカル。

　ついでに周囲の言う通り、二年連続ミス峰城大付とか、学園ナンバーワンアイドルとか、撃墜王とか色々と派手な肩書きを持つ完璧な美少女。

「どっちにしても、あの小木曽がお前の目の前で笑顔でこくんと首を縦に振るなんて、そんなありえない妄想話なんか聞きたくないんだよ俺たちは」

「いや、でも本当にあっさり引き受けてくれたんだってば……」
lines.english:
Because of “certain circumstances,” Haruki had not spoken to her until his third year—and might soon find himself involved with her far more deeply…

More plainly, she was the newest member of Haruki’s Light Music Club.

She was the even more hastily acquired vocalist for a pickup band due to perform at the school festival one month from now.

She was also, as everyone kept pointing out, a perfect beauty with a whole collection of gaudy titles: Miss Houjou High two years running, the most popular girl in school, the undisputed queen of rejection.

“Either way, we don’t want to hear some impossible fantasy where that Ogiso smiles at you and gives you a sweet little nod.”

“But she really did say yes that easily…”

lines.japanese:
もちろん嘘だ。

　雪菜が春希の申し出に首を縦に振るまでには、確かに様々な苦労と紆余曲折と意外な展開が目白押しだった。

　けれどそれは、多分、周囲が想像するような経緯とはかけ離れた内容だったから説明のしようがなかっただけで……

　何しろ春希の知っている雪菜は、皆の知っている小木曽とは全然違う、地味に生きようとしても世間が許さなくて色々としがらみに振り回されているという、なかなかにシンパシーを感じさせる苦労人なのだから。
lines.english:
That, of course, was a lie.

Before Setsuna finally nodded yes to Haruki’s proposal, there had been no shortage of trouble, twists, turns, and unexpected developments.

But the story bore so little resemblance to anything his classmates might imagine that he had no idea how to explain it…

The Setsuna Haruki knew was nothing like the Ogiso they knew. She was a hard-luck girl who tried to keep her head down, only for the world to refuse to let her, forever dragged this way and that by other people’s expectations—and remarkably easy for him to identify with.

lines.japanese:
「それにさ、まだ浮かれてる場合じゃないんだってば」

「なんでよ？　小木曽が歌うんだろ？」

「そんなのもう勝ったも同然じゃん。お前らの出番の時だけ人で溢れ返るぞ絶対」

「そりゃまぁ、ボーカルは文句のつけようがなくなったよ。けどその他が……」
lines.english:
“Besides, this still isn’t the time to celebrate.”

“Why not? Ogiso’s singing, isn’t she?”

“You’ve practically won already. The place will be packed to bursting for your set, guaranteed.”

“Sure, there’s nothing left to worry about in the vocal department. But the rest of the band…”

lines.japanese:
「………」

　その台詞とともに、春希がちらり、と視線を向けた先には、窓際の席で突っ伏している女生徒の姿があった。
lines.english:
“…”

As he spoke, Haruki glanced toward the girl slumped over a desk beside the window.

lines.japanese:
この、始業から終業まで教室で眠りこけ、一部を除いたクラスメイトに空気扱いされているのは……そう、その少女こそ、名前を冬馬かずさという。

　変わり者とか、浮いた存在とか、孤高の一匹狼とか色々と微妙な肩書きを持つおかげで、誰からも距離を置かれている、単なる厄介者な美少女。

　今もその評判が示す通り、周囲の喧騒など何処吹く風で、何事にも興味なさそうに安らかな寝息を立てていた。

　……と、周囲に信じ込ませることができているのも、いつもの不良じみた言動のお陰だった。

「………」

　実は、さっきから全然寝ていなかった。というか、寝てなんかいられなかった。

　先ほどから、隣の男子たちが口にする『小木曽雪菜』という名前が、いちいちかずさの神経に障ってきていたから。
lines.english:
The girl who slept in the classroom from the first bell to the last, treated as invisible by all but a few of her classmates, was—yes, none other than Kazusa Touma.

Thanks to a collection of dubious titles—oddball, outcast, lone wolf—everyone kept their distance from this beautiful nuisance.

True to her reputation, she seemed oblivious to the surrounding uproar, breathing peacefully in sleep as if nothing in the world interested her.

Or so she had everyone convinced, helped along by her usual delinquent ways.

“…”

In truth, she had not been asleep at all. She could not possibly have slept.

Every fresh mention of the name “Setsuna Ogiso” by the boys beside her was getting on Kazusa’s nerves all over again.

lines.japanese:
“とある事情”で、かずさが三年生になって以下略な相手……

　とはいえ、かずさは彼女の存在だけは……いや、同じ学園の誰もがその名を知らないでいる方が難しかった。

　向かいの校舎の窓や、登下校の通学路……というか、人の輪の真ん中を見れば大抵そこにいる。

　目を逸らそうにも、周囲の視線が全部同じ方向を向くものだからつられずにはいられない。

　誰もが好意を抱かずにはいられないその笑顔。

　周囲を和ませ、そして華やかにする雰囲気の良さ。

　そしてほんの少し垂れ気味の丸く見開かれた瞳に代表される柔らかな可愛らしさ。
lines.english:
Because of “certain circumstances,” Kazusa had, in her third year… et cetera.

Still, Kazusa had always known she existed—no, it was hard for anyone at the school not to know her name.

Through the windows of the building opposite, on the way to and from school… or, really, one only had to look toward the center of any crowd and she would usually be there.

Even trying to look elsewhere was useless when every other gaze pointed the same way; your own eyes inevitably followed.

That smile, impossible not to like.

Her gift for putting everyone around her at ease and making every place brighter.

And the gentle prettiness embodied by her wide, round eyes, their outer corners drooping ever so slightly.

lines.japanese:
同じ学年で、いや、同じ学園で彼女に関心を持たないとしたらその人物は……冬馬かずさのような厭世的なサボリ魔に違いない。

　いや、違う。

　―なんなんだ、あいつは。

　何しろ今は、そのかずさですら小木曽雪菜のことには並々ならぬ関心を持たざるを得ない状況に追い込まれているのだから。

　数日前、彼女と初めて会話とも言えないような二言三言を交わしたときのことを思い出す。
lines.english:
Anyone in their year—no, anyone in the school—who took no interest in her would have to be a world-weary chronic slacker like Kazusa Touma.

Except that was wrong.

—What the hell is with her?

Circumstances had now forced even Kazusa to take far more interest in Setsuna Ogiso than she wanted.

She remembered the two or three words they had exchanged a few days earlier—if that could even be called a conversation.

lines.japanese:
小木曽雪菜は……やはり、周囲が言う通りのアイドルだった。

　昔から聞いていた評判通り、目にしていたイメージ通りの、可愛い顔、声、仕草から繰り出される明るく爽やかな態度でかずさと、その場にいた彼女のバンド仲間に接していた。

　ただ、ほんの少しだけ評判と違っていたのは、その距離感。

　それも当然かずさとのではなく、彼女のバンド仲間との……

「……」

　あの時かずさは、絶対に合わないタイプだと直感で悟った。

　何もかも自分と違う、光の、白の、太陽の属性。

　いい意味で特別扱いされ続けてきた、正しく強い勇者。

　相手に対しての気持ちを正直に顔に出せる、そのまっすぐな心。

　だから彼女はかずさにとって、今年に入って二人目の、苦手な奴になった。

　他人に関心を持たないかずさには、他人を苦手とする理由などないはずなのに……
lines.english:
Setsuna Ogiso had been… every inch the golden girl everyone claimed.

Everything about her—the pretty face and voice, the charming gestures—matched both her reputation and the impression Kazusa had already formed of her; so did the bright, open warmth with which she had treated Kazusa and the bandmate beside her.

Only one tiny detail differed from that reputation: the easy familiarity in her manner.

Not toward Kazusa, of course, but toward the bandmate with her…

“…”

Kazusa had known at once that Setsuna was the sort of person she could never get along with.

She was all light and white and sun, the opposite of Kazusa in every conceivable way.

A hero, righteous and strong, who had always been treated as someone special—in a good way.

An honest, forthright heart that let her show people exactly how she felt.

And so Setsuna became the second person that year Kazusa found herself unable to handle.

Yet someone with no interest in other people ought to have no one she couldn’t handle…

lines.japanese:
「あれ、冬馬、どこいくんだ？」

「っ……」

　なんとなく苛ついた頭を冷やしてこようと席を立ったかずさに、まるでずっと観察していたかのようにすぐ声をかけてきたのは、ついさっきまで騒動の中心にいた、今年に入って一人目な奴だった。

「もうすぐ昼休み終わるぞ？　昼飯食べないのか？」

「……委員長ってのはクラスの人間の栄養状態にまで気を配らなくちゃならないのか、そりゃ大変だな」

「そういう訳じゃないけど、きちんと三食摂らないと余計に眠くなるぞ」

「そうだよ。眠いんだから話しかけるな鬱陶しい」

「冬馬……」
lines.english:
“Touma? Where are you going?”

“—!”

Feeling vaguely irritated, Kazusa had risen to clear her head. The person who called out at once—as though he had been watching her all along—was the first person that year she had found herself unable to handle, and until moments ago had been the center of all the commotion.

“Lunch break’s almost over. Aren’t you going to eat?”

“Does being class representative mean keeping tabs on everyone’s nutrition too? Must be exhausting.”

“Not exactly, but if you don’t eat three proper meals a day, you’ll only get sleepier.”

“Exactly. I’m sleepy, so stop talking to me. You’re annoying.”

“Touma…”

lines.japanese:
と、かずさは彼に向かって、いつも以上の冷たい視線と声で歓迎してみせる。

　それは間違いなくかずさらしい理不尽な態度だったけれど、彼女にしてみれば、それくらいの憂さ晴らしはさせてもらえないとやってられないという心境だった。

　だって彼こそが、今のかずさの不機嫌の諸悪の根元だったから。

　かずさの前に、水と油としか思えない雪菜を連れてきた。

　変に興奮した口調で雪菜のことを熱く語った。

　雪菜がバンドを、自分を救ってくれたって。

　雪菜だけが、自分の味方なんだって。

　雪菜、だけ、って……
lines.english:
Kazusa welcomed him with a look and a voice even colder than usual.

It was unmistakably unreasonable and unmistakably Kazusa, but as far as she was concerned, if she couldn’t vent at least that much, she would never stand it.

After all, he was the root cause of her foul mood.

He had brought Setsuna, who should have mixed with Kazusa about as well as oil with water, right in front of her.

He had rhapsodized about Setsuna in a strangely excited voice.

Setsuna had saved the band. Saved him.

Setsuna was the only one on his side.

Setsuna. Only Setsuna…

lines.japanese:
「？　顔色悪いな。冬馬、お前もしかして体調が……」

「っ……な、なんでもないから、寄るな！」

「あ……」

　こちらを心配してくれたはずの春希の手をふりほどくと、かずさは逃げるように教室を出ていく。

　自分の考えていたことが、なんだか変にむず痒くて気持ち悪かったから。

　僻むことには慣れているはずなのに、その僻みの内容がいつものとあまりに乖離していたから。
lines.english:
“You look pale. Touma, are you feeling—?”

“I-I’m fine! Stay away from me!”

“Ah…”

Though Haruki had surely only reached out because he was worried, Kazusa shook off his hand and all but fled the classroom.

What she had caught herself thinking made her skin crawl.

Resentment was nothing new to her. It was what she resented this time that felt so grotesquely unlike the usual kind.

lines.japanese:
「あ……」

　少し強く扉を閉めて廊下に出た瞬間、かずさは吐きかけたため息を一瞬で呑み込んだ。

「あ……」

　目的地である３年Ｅ組の教室の手前で、雪菜は息を呑むと共に歩みを止めた。

「……」

「……」

　十歩ほどの距離を置いて、お互い、相手に目を奪われていた。
lines.english:
“Ah…”

The instant Kazusa shut the door a little too hard and stepped into the hall, she swallowed the sigh already on her lips.

“Ah…”

Just short of her destination, Class 3-E, Setsuna caught her breath and stopped walking.

“…”

“…”

Ten paces apart, each stood transfixed by the other.

lines.japanese:
―冬馬、さん

　―小木曽、雪菜

　二人とも、相手が自分を見ていることをしっかり意識しながらも、自分の視線が相手を向いてしまっていることには気づかない。

　だから自分がさり気なく振る舞えていると信じて、ふたたびゆっくりと、けれど今度はぎこちなく歩き出す。

　相手の方へと、向かって。
lines.english:
—Touma…

—Setsuna… Ogiso.

Both were acutely aware of being watched. Neither realized she was doing precisely the same thing.

Each convinced she looked perfectly casual, they began walking again, slowly as before but awkward now.

Straight toward each other.

lines.japanese:
―やっぱり、カッコいいなぁ

　雪菜は、ついついかずさと自分とを見比べてしまう。

　身長があと３センチ高かったらといつも思っていたのに、目の前の同級生は、自分よりも５センチほど高くて。

　髪も、自分のはこれ以上伸ばすと先が跳ねてしまうのに、目の前にサラサラと流れる黒髪は、自分よりも１０センチは長くて。

　そしてあと、せめてもう１サイズ増やしたいと思っているカップは……
lines.english:
—She really is so cool…

Setsuna could not help measuring herself against Kazusa.

She was forever wishing she were three centimeters taller, yet the girl before her stood a good five centimeters taller than she did.

Her own hair would flip out at the ends if she grew it any longer, yet the sleek black hair flowing past her was at least ten centimeters longer than hers.

And then there was her own bust, which she always wished were at least one cup size larger…

lines.japanese:
―可愛い、って、こういうのを言うんだろうな

　かずさは、雪菜の立ち振る舞いに、言い知れぬ理不尽さを感じる。

　全体的に作りの大きい自分に比べて、黄金比とはこういうことだと言わんばかりの絶妙のバランス。

　人をビビらせることしか能のない自分の目つきに比べて、人を惹きつけずにはいられない、ちょっと上目遣い気味の大きく澄んだ瞳。

　そして何より、とある情報筋から幾度も聞かされた、見た目だけでは測れない、彼女の本当の魅力……

　そんな、どう考えても不躾な視線を互いに感じつつ、それでも互いに無関心を装い。
lines.english:
—That must be what cute looks like.

Kazusa found something profoundly unfair in the very way Setsuna carried herself.

Next to Kazusa’s oversized build, Setsuna was balanced so exquisitely she might have been a demonstration of the golden ratio.

Next to Kazusa’s glare, good for nothing but frightening people, those huge, clear eyes, always seeming to look slightly upward at whoever they met, could not help drawing people in.

Then, beyond any of that, there was the charm no outward glance could measure: the charm a certain source had gone on about more than once…

Each could feel the outrageous rudeness of the other’s scrutiny. Each continued pretending not to care.

lines.japanese:
「……」

「……」

　十秒にも満たない、十時間にも感じる十歩は、過ぎ去った。

　すれ違う際、なぜか二人とも、その表情にほんの少しの敗北感を漂わせつつ。

　そして、そのままかずさは突き当たりの階段を上り……

「……はぁ」

　雪菜はＥ組の教室の扉へと手をかけながら……

「……ん～」

　二人が廊下から消えるほんの一瞬。

　最後に振り返った時、相手は自分のことを見ていなかった。
lines.english:
“…”

“…”

The ten paces passed in less than ten seconds and felt more like ten hours.

As they crossed, both wore a faint, inexplicable look of defeat.

Kazusa continued on and climbed the stairs at the end of the corridor…

“…Hah.”

Setsuna put her hand to the door of Class 3-E…

“…Mmm.”

For one brief instant before both vanished from the corridor,

each cast one last glance back—and found that the other was not looking.

lines.japanese:
けれどそれは、ほんの少しのタイムラグ。

　どちらが先に振り返ったか、どちらが最後まで相手を見ていたかの、どっちにしても一勝一敗のチキンレース。

　なのに、その勝敗を判定する審判がこの場にいないせいで、意味のない敗北感と理由のわからない疲労が、二人同時に、ますます重くのしかかる。

　それでも、いつまでもそうやって原因のわからないままもやもやした気持ちを抱えつづける訳にもいかず、二人はほぼ同時に呟く。
lines.english:
Yet it was only a fraction of a second’s mismatch.

Which had turned first, and which had watched the other to the very end? Either way, their game of chicken had ended at one win apiece.

But no referee had been there to call the result. The same meaningless sense of defeat and inexplicable exhaustion settled ever more heavily on them both.

They could not go on indefinitely nursing this restless feeling without knowing its cause, and so, almost simultaneously, each murmured:

lines.japanese:
「よしっ」

　雪菜は、小さく握った拳に力を込めて。
lines.english:
“All right!”

Setsuna clenched one small fist.

lines.japanese:
「……よし」

　かずさは、窓から空を見上げて。
lines.english:
“…All right.”

Kazusa looked up at the sky through the window.

lines.japanese:
―話しかけてみようっと

　―関わり合いになるのはやめよう

　お互いに、小さな決意を胸に秘め。
lines.english:
—I’m going to talk to her.

—I’m going to stay away from her.

Each kept her small resolution to herself.
